data.title: Provider Credentialing and Practice Lead
data.description:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

The Clinical Practicec Lead owns practice management for Neko Health's United States professional corporation. The role covers four areas: provider credentialing, SOP organization and maintenance, onboarding operationalization, and compliance assurance. Neko runs a tech-enabled clinical model, and this role is expected to run all four through systems and automation rather than manual tracking.

Credentialing: the role holds the credential file for every provider practicing under the PC: license, certification, permitted scope by state, malpractice coverage details and every other expirable, verified at source and kept current so that no provider ever sees a member on a lapsed credential. While Neko does not credential with payers today - this role runs the credentialing gate that clears a provider to practice and removes that clearance when a credential lapses. It supplies provider credentialing data into the clinic compliance systems and works to the credentialing standard and clear-to-practice definition set by the Head of Compliance.

SOPs: the role owns the SOP library for US practice operations. The role keeps every SOP current, versioned, and easy to find, and retires SOPs that no longer apply.

Onboarding: the role turns each new provider's onboarding plan into a working, tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start, in the right order and against a clear timeline.

Compliance: the role checks that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance, and reports gaps as they surface.

Systems and automation: the role chooses, configures and owns the tooling that carries all of the above — one source of truth for provider data, automated expiry alerts, and workflows that hand off cleanly between Talent Acquisition, the People Team, IT and clinical operations. Status should be visible from the system rather than assembled by hand.

As Neko opens further states, credentialing volume and complexity grow faster than headcount, and practice operations grow with them. This role exists to make provider readiness, SOP currency, onboarding execution, and compliance standing a managed process with evidence behind it, built on tooling that scales faster than headcount, rather than a scramble before each launch.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • A current, auditable register of every clinician's license, credential, and permitted scope by state, held in a single system of record with automated expiry tracking and a named process for renewal before lapse.

  • A complete credential file per provider practicing under the PC, with primary source verification evidence attached and dated.

  • A written credentialing procedure covering intake, verification, the clear-to-practice decision, re-verification cycle, and removal of clearance.

  • The credentialing gate built into the clinician onboarding sequence, so a start date cannot be confirmed without verified credentials.

  • A current SOP library for US practice operations: indexed, version-controlled, and reviewed on a set cycle.

  • An onboarding operations sequence that turns each new provider's plan into a tracked timeline from offer to start, with the credentialing gate built in.

  • Practice operations running in-system rather than on spreadsheets: onboarding, SOP review cycles and compliance checks tracked in Neko's tooling, with the remaining manual steps documented and a plan to remove them.

  • A compliance status report showing where US practice operations meet the Head of Compliance's standards, and where they do not, generated from the system rather than compiled by hand.

Key Responsibilities

Provider credentialing and primary source verification

  • Run credentialing intake for every new provider joining the PC: application, document collection, and verification at source rather than from candidate-supplied copies.

  • Verify state medical/nursing licenses, board certification, education and training, work history, and DEA registration where the provider's scope requires it.

  • Operate the clear-to-practice gate: no provider is released to see members until the credential file is complete and verified.

  • Maintain the permitted scope by state for each provider and flag to the Head of Compliance any request to practice outside it.

Expirables, re-verification and removal

  • Own the expirables calendar for licenses, certifications, DEA registrations, malpractice coverage and any other time-limited credential, driven by automated alerts rather than manual review.

  • Chase renewals ahead of expiry against defined lead times and escalate when a renewal is at risk.

  • Remove clearance to practice immediately when a credential lapses and notify the clinical rota owner and the Head of Compliance the same day.

  • Run the re-verification cycle so credential files do not silently age.

Systems, tooling and automation

  • Select, implement and administer the tooling that runs practice operations: credentialing records, expiry tracking, onboarding workflow and SOP version control.

  • Replace manual tracking with automated alerts, scheduled reporting and system-driven handoffs, and keep a running list of the steps still done by hand.

  • Define the data structure behind credentialing and onboarding so status can be reported out of the system rather than reconstructed.

  • Work with IT and, where relevant, product and engineering to integrate practice operations data with adjacent systems instead of maintaining parallel spreadsheets.

SOP organization and maintenance

  • Own the SOP library for US practice operations: create, index, and version every procedure.

  • Review each SOP on a set cycle and update it when a process changes.

  • Retire SOPs that no longer apply, and flag processes that run without one.

  • Keep SOPs easy to find and use for the staff who rely on them day to day.

Onboarding operationalization

  • Turn each new provider's onboarding plan into a tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start.

  • Own the onboarding timeline from offer to start date, and flag delays before they hit the start date.

  • Coordinate with Talent Acquisition, the People Team, and clinical operations to keep the sequence moving.

  • Improve the onboarding sequence as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

Compliance assurance

  • Confirm that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance.

  • Run periodic checks against those standards, and report gaps as they surface.

  • Support audits of practice operations with evidence drawn from SOPs, onboarding records, and the credentialing file.

  • Escalate compliance gaps that need action beyond this role.

Credentialing process, data and reporting

  • Keep the credentialing record system accurate and audit-ready, so a credential file can be produced on request without reconstruction.

  • Report credentialing status, upcoming expiries and blocked providers into the Medical Quality reporting cycle, on a set cadence and drawn from the system of record.

  • Improve the credentialing process as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.

  • Prepare the function for payer credentialing and provider enrollment should Neko US move to billing insurance.

About you

Minimum Requirements

  • Experience streamlining clinical or healthcare operations in a tech-enabled environment: you have taken a manual, spreadsheet-run process and rebuilt it as a system-driven workflow, and you can describe what you removed and what changed as a result.

  • Experience working in a clinical operations capacity – where you were responsible for not just executing but building the systems to ensure credentialing, compliance and other clinical operations processes are handled excellently.

  • Confident with operational tooling: you configure and administer the systems you depend on rather than raising a ticket for every change, and you are comfortable working with data, reporting and everyday automation.

  • Direct, hands-on experience of state medical board licensure and clinician credentialing processes, including primary source verification.

  • Experience maintaining a credentialing database or record system to an audit-ready standard.

  • Experience developing, organizing, and maintaining SOPs in a clinical or regulated operations setting.

  • Working knowledge of compliance standards in a healthcare or clinical operations setting, with experience checking operations against them.

  • Precise and persistent administratively

Preferred

  • Experience in a digital health, telehealth or otherwise tech-enabled care setting, where clinical operations run on product and tooling rather than paper.

  • Hands-on experience with credentialing or provider data platforms, and with the workflow and tracking tools used to run operations day to day.

  • Experience working alongside product or engineering teams to specify what operational tooling needs to do.

  • Direct experience provider credentialing in a United States clinical setting, including multi-state credentialing.

  • Experience of credentialing in a newly opened market or a start-up clinical service where the process did not yet exist.

  • Experience building an SOP program from scratch in a growing or newly opened operation.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Paid Time Off & Holidays

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan

  • Commuter Benefits

  • Wellness Rewards Program

  • Complimentary full Neko scan for you and eligible family members

Compensation: $137K – $167K

data.title: Project Manager - Software Implementation (m/f/x)
data.description:
Job Title: Project Manager - Software Implementation (m/f/x) 

Location: EU

(Remote) 

 

Who You’ll Work For: 

 

At Makersite, we're pioneering the future of sustainable product development and digital collaboration. As a leading platform for product lifecycle management (PLM), we empower companies to make smarter, more sustainable decisions across their entire supply chain. Our cutting-edge software enables teams to design, prototype, and manufacture with transparency, efficiency, and responsibility—reducing environmental impact while optimizing performance. 

We're a fast-growing, innovative company that thrives on creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning. If you're passionate about technology, sustainability, and creating meaningful impact, we’d love to hear from you. Join us and be a part of shaping the future of manufacturing and product innovation. 

 

Who we're looking for: 

 

As part of our growing team, you will play a key role in shaping the future of sustainable product development. We’re looking for innovative, driven Project Managers who are passionate about technology and sustainability to join us in building tools that enable companies to make smarter, more responsible decisions. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to collaborate with talented professionals, contribute to cutting-edge projects, and help drive the digital transformation of industries worldwide. If you're ready to make an impact and contribute to meaningful change, we want to hear from you! 

This role is a fixed, permanent position. All successful applicants will receive a permanent employment contract regardless of location.  

 

The role:

  

  • Lead the planning and implementation of software projects related to system connections with our customers, ensuring they are delivered on time and within scope. 

  • Maintain and update project plans, proactively identifying and managing any project risks. 

  • Ensure the availability of the right expertise for each project phase, coordinating with internal and external resources as necessary. 

  • Manage stakeholder expectations, delivering regular and comprehensive project updates and effectively resolving any arising issues. 

  • Contribute to the standardization of project implementation methodology and project templates to improve project standardization and efficiency. 

  • Generate thorough Project/Solution Documentation, outlining project goals, deliverables, and timelines. 

  • Handle all customer communication across various projects, ensuring clear, consistent, and timely communication with all stakeholders. 


  • Master's degree in project management or related technical field required. 

  • Background in Electronics/Electricals

  • Professional Project Management Certification from an accredited institution preferred. 

  • Demonstrated understanding of Project Management processes, strategies, and methods 

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills and experience establishing guidelines in these areas for others. 

  • 3+ years of Project management experience in the field of software implementations 

  • Experience with complex data projects where a systematic approach is crucial to success. 

  • Dexterity with software tools and data manipulation & analysis 

  • A creative mind that can think outside the box. 

  • Curiosity to find disruptive as opposed to incremental solutions to challenging data problems. 

  • Residing in and legally permitted to work in the EU. 

 

What We Offer: 

 

  • Competitive Salary – We reward your skills and experience with a compensation package that reflects your value. 

  • 30 Days Paid Time Off – Take the time you need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance. 

  • Remote-First Flexibility – Work from anywhere in the EU, with the option to collaborate in person at our offices in Stuttgart, Berlin (role dependent). 

  • Generous Learning & Development Budget – We invest in your growth, providing ample resources for personal and professional development. 

  • Choose Your Ideal Work Equipment – Whether you prefer Apple or Microsoft, we’ll equip you with the tools you need to excel. 

 

The Experience: 

 

  • Purpose-Driven Work – Build something meaningful. Here, you’re not just creating another app; you’re contributing to a transformative vision that you can be proud of. 

  • Great Colleagues – Join a team that’s open, transparent, and international. We value inclusivity and foster a culture of collaboration and mutual respect. 

  • Work-Life Balance – As a remote-first company, we trust you to do your best work, your way. You have the flexibility to work when it suits you, ensuring a healthy balance between personal and professional life. 

  • Pride in Impact – We're already making a significant difference with global, well-known customers who share our vision. Be part of something that matters. 

  • Stability with Ambition – With realistic growth plans, we’re committed to changing the way things are made—without sacrificing our ambitious goals for innovation and impact. 

If you want to find out more about what it’s like to work at Makersite, check out our Careers Page here 

  

Diversity and Inclusion 

If you have a medical condition or an individual need for an adjustment to our process, and you believe this may affect your ability to be at your best – please let us know so we can talk about how we can best support you and make any adjustments that may be needed.  

 

At Makersite, we are dedicated to fostering an environment that champions diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We believe that diverse teams drive innovation and success, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and will consider all applications regardless of age, disability, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy or maternity, race, nationality, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable law. Rest assured, all applications will be handled with the utmost confidentiality.

data.title: Management Accountant
data.description:
About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We’re creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why This Role

We're seeking a bilingual Management Accountant to serve as the cornerstone of our German accounting operations. This role combines hands-on accounting execution with strategic financial operations, ensuring seamless coordination between our German and US entities while maintaining compliance with both German and US GAAP standards.

You'll work at the intersection of day-to-day financial operations and cross-border business requirements, partnering closely with our Head of Finance, People Operations, external payroll providers, and local German accounting advisors to maintain accurate, timely financial reporting across our dual-entity structure.

What You’ll Work On

Core Accounting Operations

  • Manage full-cycle billing, collections, and accounts payable for German entity

  • Execute treasury and cash management functions, including inter-company settlements

  • Process and reconcile inter-company transactions between German and US entities

  • Partner with People Operations and external payroll agencies across Europe to ensure accurate and timely payroll accounting entries

  • Review payroll outputs from external providers and post journal entries to the general ledger

  • Reconcile payroll-related balance sheet accounts (accruals, statutory deductions, benefits) each month

  • Maintain accurate books and records in accordance with German GAAP (HGB)

  • Maintain dual bookkeeping across DATEV (German statutory books) and Rillet (global ERP), ensuring both systems remain accurate, aligned, and reconciled on an ongoing basis

Tax & Compliance

  • Coordinate with external German accountants (Steuerberater) to ensure accurate VAT returns and filings

  • Support annual tax compliance including Körperschaftsteuer and Gewerbesteuer

  • Maintain documentation for tax audits and statutory requirements

  • Monitor regulatory changes affecting German accounting and tax obligations

US GAAP Reporting Support

  • Assist in reconciling German GAAP accounts to US GAAP basis

  • Provide monthly financial data and schedules for consolidated US GAAP reporting

  • Support quarter-end and year-end close processes for global consolidation

  • Help maintain documentation for US GAAP accounting policies and procedures

Process & Systems

  • Implement and improve accounting processes and internal controls

  • Work with ERP and financial systems to enhance efficiency and accuracy

  • Support integration of German operations into global financial infrastructure

  • Maintain organized documentation for internal and external stakeholders

What We’re Looking For:

  • Education: Completed Ausbildung as Steuerfachangestellter/ Steuerfachwirt or similar accounting qualification; Bachelor's degree in Finance/Accounting preferred

  • Experience: 3 plus years experience in accounting role(s), preferably in fast-growing companies or startups

  • Language: Full fluency in both German and English is a core requirement

  • Technical: Strong proficiency with accounting software and Excel; experience with ERP systems

  • Location: Based in or willing to relocate to Freiburg, Germany

While not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Experience with DATEV and/or modern cloud ERP systems (e.g., Rillet, NetSuite)

  • Familiarity with both German GAAP (HGB) and US GAAP principles

  • Experience working in dual-entity or international company structures

  • Prior work with German Steuerberater and understanding of VAT compliance

  • Experience coordinating with People Operations and third-party payroll providers (rather than running payroll directly)

  • Experience in technology or SaaS companies

  • Knowledge of intercompany accounting and transfer pricing basics

How We Work Together

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. Depending on your role, you’ll either join us in Freiburg or SF at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week), or work remotely with a monthly in-person week to stay connected. We’ll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we’ve structured things to make it accessible to all. We’ll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

  • Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

  • Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

  • Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.

Base Annual Salary: EU €70,000- €100,000 + Equity

Note: Our recruitment process uses AI-assisted tools to help manage and organize applications. All hiring decisions are always made by our team.

data.title: Senior Partner
data.description:
About the Role

Join the leadership team of an AI-enabled legal services company as a Senior Partner. You will continue serving your existing clients while helping grow the practice and move suitable recurring legal work onto an AI agent platform.

What You'll Do

  • Help shape the firm's growth strategy as it expands its client base.

  • Bring your portable client relationships to the platform and continue providing legal services to those clients.

  • Build market awareness and develop new opportunities through your professional network.

  • Identify opportunities to offer commercial and compliance services to existing clients.

  • Work with the founding team to identify recurring legal matters that can be supported by AI agents.

What We're Looking For

  • 12 to 20 or more years of legal experience, with German qualification as a Volljurist.

  • A substantial, personally held and portable book of business.

  • Strong relationships with private equity firms, mid-market businesses, or similar clients, and the ability to develop related commercial and compliance work.

  • Experience with recurring legal matters, such as commercial contracts, IT and data, corporate or venture capital work, or regulatory matters. A practice focused only on litigation is not a match for the work described.

  • Native-level German for client work and professional English.

  • Interest in AI-supported legal services, including agent platforms and legal AI tools.

Compensation & Benefits

Annual salary range: €200,000 to €300,000. The role includes meaningful equity. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Location

Hybrid role based in Berlin, Germany.
